name: Wang Chih-huan
bio: Wang Chih-huan was a T’ang poet of the eighth century, whose quatrain on Heron Lodge is among the best known of its period.
The poems here are Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu’s versions in The Jade Mountain (1929), given with the poet’s name as spelled here.

poems.title: At Heron Lodge
poems.author: Wang Chih-huan
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Mountains cover the white sun,
And oceans drain the golden river;
But you widen your view three hundred miles
By going up one flight of stairs.

poems.title: Beyond the Border
poems.author: Wang Chih-huan
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Where a yellow river climbs to the white clouds,
Near the one city-wall among ten-thousand-foot mountains,
A Tartar under the willows is lamenting on his flute
That spring never blows to him through the Jade Pass.

poems.title: 登鸛雀樓 (Deng guan que lou)
poems.author: Wang Chih-huan
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
白日依山盡，黃河入海流。
欲窮千里目，更上一層樓。

poems.title: 涼州詞二首·其一 (Liang zhou ci er shou, qi yi)
poems.author: Wang Chih-huan
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
黃河遠上白雲間，一片孤城萬仞山。
羌笛何須怨楊柳，春風不度玉門關。
